## Set $f(x)$ equal to 4 and rearrange
3x^2 - 6x + 7 &= 4
3x^2 - 6x + 3 &= 0
## Factorise and solve
3(x^2 - 2x + 1) &= 0
3(x - 1)(x - 1) &= 0
(x - 1)^2 &= 0
x - 1 &= 0
x &= 1
ANSWER: x = 1

## Differentiate $f(x)$
f(x) &= 3x^2 - 6x + 7
f'(x) &= 6x - 6
## Set the derivative equal to 0 to find the turning point
6x - 6 &= 0
6x &= 6
x &= 1
## Find the $y$-co-ordinate
f(1) &= 3(1)^2 - 6(1) + 7
&= 3 - 6 + 7
&= 4
## Check that it is a minimum
f''(x) &= 6
$f''(1) = 6 > 0$, so the turning point is a local minimum.
ANSWER: (1, 4)

## Set the two common differences equal
In an arithmetic sequence, $T_2 - T_1 = T_3 - T_2$.
k - (-5) &= 1 - k
k + 5 &= 1 - k
## Solve for k
k + k &= 1 - 5
2k &= -4
k &= -2
## Show the common difference is 3
d &= k - (-5)
&= -2 + 5
&= 3
ANSWER: k = -2, \quad d = 3

## Write down a and d
The first term is $a = -5$ and the common difference is $d = 3$.
## Use the formula for the nth term
T_n &= a + (n-1)d
T_{10} &= -5 + (10-1)(3)
&= -5 + (9)(3)
&= -5 + 27
&= 22
ANSWER: T_{10} = 22

## Set the nth term equal to 247
T_n &= a + (n-1)d
-5 + (n-1)(3) &= 247
## Solve for n
-5 + 3n - 3 &= 247
3n - 8 &= 247
3n &= 255
n &= 85
ANSWER: n = 85 \text{ (the 85th term)}

## Write down a and d
The terms go 4, 9, 14, so $a = 4$ and $d = 9 - 4 = 5$.
## Substitute into the sum formula
S_n &= \frac{n}{2}\left[2a + (n-1)d\right]
S_{50} &= \frac{50}{2}\left[2(4) + (50-1)(5)\right]
&= 25\left[8 + (49)(5)\right]
&= 25\left[8 + 245\right]
&= 25(253)
&= 6325
ANSWER: S_{50} = 6325

## Add the three bands
The top rate starts once the first three bands are used up.
12\,012 + 8472 + 49\,560 &= 20\,484 + 49\,560
&= 70\,044
ANSWER: \text{€}70\,044

## USC on the first two bands
John earns more than $12\,012 + 8472$, so the first two bands are full. From part (b):
0.5\% \text{ of } 12\,012 &= 60.06
2\% \text{ of } 8472 &= 169.44
## Find the income in the 4.5% band
54\,800 - (12\,012 + 8472) &= 54\,800 - 20\,484
&= 34\,316
## USC on €34 316 at 4.5%
4.5\% \text{ of } 34\,316 &= \frac{4.5}{100} \times 34\,316
&= 1544.22
## Add the three amounts
60.06 + 169.44 + 1544.22 &= 229.50 + 1544.22
&= 1773.72
ANSWER: \text{€}1773.72

## Subtract the USC on the first two bands
Mary pays more than $60.06 + 169.44$, so she is in the 4.5% band.
1602.72 - (60.06 + 169.44) &= 1602.72 - 229.50
&= 1373.22
## Find the income taxed at 4.5%
Let $x$ be the income in the 4.5% band.
0.045x &= 1373.22
x &= \frac{1373.22}{0.045}
x &= 30\,516
## Add the income in the lower bands
\text{Income} &= 12\,012 + 8472 + 30\,516
&= 20\,484 + 30\,516
&= 51\,000
ANSWER: \text{€}51\,000

## Find the USC paid at the top rate
Patrick earns more than €70 044, so he pays the full USC from the first three bands: €2459.70 (part (b)).
3496.18 - 2459.70 &= 1036.48
## Find the income taxed at the top rate
83\,000 - 70\,044 &= 12\,956
## Divide to find the rate
\text{Rate} &= \frac{1036.48}{12\,956} \times 100
&= 8
&= 8\%
ANSWER: 8\%

## Read the dimensions from the diagram
A square of side $x$ is cut from each corner, so $x$ is removed from both ends of each 10-unit side.
l &= 10 - x - x
&= 10 - 2x
b &= 10 - 2x
The height is the folded-up side of a cut-out square.
h &= x
ANSWER: l = 10 - 2x, \quad b = 10 - 2x, \quad h = x

## Write the volume as length times breadth times height
V &= l \times b \times h
V &= (10-2x)(10-2x)(x)
## Multiply out the first two brackets
(10-2x)(10-2x) &= 100 - 20x - 20x + 4x^2
&= 100 - 40x + 4x^2
## Multiply by x
V &= x(100 - 40x + 4x^2)
&= 100x - 40x^2 + 4x^3
&= 4x^3 - 40x^2 + 100x
ANSWER: V(x) = 4x^3 - 40x^2 + 100x

## Test the breadth when the height is 6
The height is $h = x$, so a height of 6 means $x = 6$. The breadth $10 - 2x$ must be positive.
b &= 10 - 2(6)
&= 10 - 12
&= -2
A breadth of $-2$ is impossible. Two squares of side 6 would need 12 units, but the sheet is only 10 wide.
ANSWER: \text{Breadth } = -2 < 0, \text{ so the box is impossible}

## (i) Find the maximum volume
Draw a horizontal line level with the highest point of the curve and read across to the V axis.
V_{\max} &\approx 74
## (ii) Find x when the volume is 30
Draw a horizontal line at $V = 30$. Where it crosses the curve, drop vertical lines down to the x axis.
x &\approx 0.35 \text{ and } x \approx 3.55
## (iii) Find the volume when x = 2.8
Draw a vertical line up from $x = 2.8$ to the curve, then across to the V axis.
V(2.8) &\approx 54
Check: $V(2.8) = 4(2.8)^3 - 40(2.8)^2 + 100(2.8)$.
V(2.8) &= 87.808 - 313.6 + 280
&= 54.208
&\approx 54
ANSWER: \text{(i) } 74 \quad \text{(ii) } x = 0.35 \text{ and } x = 3.55 \quad \text{(iii) } 54

## Spot how patterns 1, 2 and 3 grow
Pattern $n$ has one row of $n$ dots above $n$ rows of $n$ crosses.
Pattern 3 has 3 dots and a 3 by 3 block of crosses.
## Draw pattern 4
Draw 4 dots in a row, with a 4 by 4 block of crosses below.
\text{Crosses} &= 4 \times 4
&= 16
ANSWER: 4 \text{ dots and } 16 \text{ crosses}

## Write down the number of dots in each pattern
Dots: 1, 2, 3, ... This is arithmetic with $a = 1$ and $d = 1$.
## Use the formula for the nth term
T_n &= a + (n-1)d
T_n &= 1 + (n-1)(1)
&= 1 + n - 1
&= n
ANSWER: T_n = n

## Use the sum formula with a = 1, d = 1 and n = 20
S_n &= \frac{n}{2}\left[2a + (n-1)d\right]
S_{20} &= \frac{20}{2}\left[2(1) + (20-1)(1)\right]
&= 10\left[2 + 19\right]
&= 10(21)
&= 210
ANSWER: S_{20} = 210

## Count the crosses in each pattern
Pattern $n$ has $n$ rows of $n$ crosses.
\text{Pattern 3: } 3 \times 3 &= 9
\text{Pattern 4: } 4 \times 4 &= 16
\text{Pattern 5: } 5 \times 5 &= 25
\text{Pattern 6: } 6 \times 6 &= 36
The completed table reads 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36.
## Write the formula
\text{Crosses} &= n \times n
&= n^2
ANSWER: n^2

## Substitute n = 12 into n squared
12^2 &= 12 \times 12
&= 144
ANSWER: 144

## Find the number of dots and crosses in pattern 10
\text{Dots} &= 10
\text{Crosses} &= 10^2
&= 100
## Add them
\text{Total} &= 10 + 100
&= 110
ANSWER: 110

## Substitute n = 1
T_1 &= \frac{1^2}{2} + b(1) + c
&= \frac{1}{2} + b + c
## Substitute n = 2
T_2 &= \frac{2^2}{2} + b(2) + c
&= \frac{4}{2} + 2b + c
&= 2 + 2b + c
ANSWER: T_1 = \frac{1}{2} + b + c, \quad T_2 = 2 + 2b + c

## Increase the flow by 10%
250\,000 \times 1.1 &= 275\,000 \text{ litres per second}
## Convert to cubic metres per second
275\,000 \div 1000 &= 275 \text{ m}^3\text{ per second}
## Multiply by the seconds in 24 hours
\text{Volume} &= 275 \times 60 \times 60 \times 24
&= 275 \times 86\,400
&= 23\,760\,000
## Write in the form a times 10 to the n
&= 2.376 \times 10^7
&\approx 2.38 \times 10^7
ANSWER: 2.38 \times 10^7 \text{ m}^3

## Count the outcomes of each spinner
The hand/foot spinner has 4 outcomes and the colour spinner has 4 outcomes.
## Multiply to get the total
\text{Outcomes} &= 4 \times 4
&= 16
ANSWER: 16

## Subtract from 1
The probabilities of success and failure add to 1.
P(\text{not knock}) &= 1 - 0.34
&= 0.66
ANSWER: 0.66

## List the three attempts
First time on the third attempt means fail, fail, then success.
## Multiply the probabilities
P &= 0.66 \times 0.66 \times 0.34
&= 0.4356 \times 0.34
&= 0.148104
&\approx 0.148
ANSWER: 0.148

## Find |AC| using Pythagoras in triangle ABC
The angle at $B$ is $90^\circ$ because $ABCF$ is a square.
|AC|^2 &= 2^2 + 2^2
&= 4 + 4
&= 8
|AC| &= \sqrt{8}
&= 2\sqrt{2}
## Find the area of the large square ACDE
\text{Square} &= |AC|^2
&= 8
## Find the area of triangle ABC
Triangle $ABC$ is half of the square $ABCF$.
\text{Triangle} &= \frac{1}{2}(2 \times 2)
&= 2
## Add the two areas
\text{Area} &= 8 + 2
&= 10 \text{ cm}^2
## Add the five outer sides for the perimeter
$AB = BC = 2$ and $CD = DE = EA = \sqrt{8}$. The side $[AC]$ is inside the figure.
\text{Perimeter} &= 2 + 2 + 3\sqrt{8}
&= 4 + 3(2\sqrt{2})
&= 4 + 6\sqrt{2}
&\approx 12.49 \text{ cm}
ANSWER: \text{Area} = 10\text{ cm}^2,\ \text{Perimeter} \approx 12.49\text{ cm}

## Find the slope from the two points
m &= \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}
&= \frac{-2 - 2}{0 - (-1)}
&= \frac{-4}{1}
&= -4
## Use the point A(-1, 2) in the line formula
y - 2 &= -4(x - (-1))
y - 2 &= -4(x + 1)
y - 2 &= -4x - 4
y &= -4x - 4 + 2
y &= -4x - 2
ANSWER: y = -4x - 2

## Find the slope of l
3x - 4y &= 5
-4y &= -3x + 5
y &= \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{5}{4}
The slope of $l$ is the coefficient of $x$, which is $\frac{3}{4}$.
## Turn it upside down and change the sign for the perpendicular slope
m_k &= -\frac{1}{3/4}
&= -\frac{4}{3}
## Use the point P(6, -3) in the line formula
y - (-3) &= -\frac{4}{3}(x - 6)
3(y + 3) &= -4(x - 6)
3y + 9 &= -4x + 24
## Rearrange into the form ax + by + c = 0
4x + 3y + 9 &= 24
4x + 3y - 15 &= 0
ANSWER: 4x + 3y - 15 = 0

## Read each point off the grid
Go across to the $x$ value first, then up or down to the $y$ value.
$A$ is at $x = 6$, $y = 2$. $B$ is at $x = -2$, $y = -4$.
ANSWER: A = (6, 2),\ B = (-2, -4)

## Use the midpoint formula
M &= \left(\frac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \frac{y_1 + y_2}{2}\right)
M &= \left(\frac{6 + (-2)}{2}, \frac{2 + (-4)}{2}\right)
&= \left(\frac{4}{2}, \frac{-2}{2}\right)
&= (2, -1)
ANSWER: (2, -1)

## Mark the centre
The centre of a circle with diameter $[AB]$ is the midpoint of $[AB]$, which is $C(2, -1)$.
## Draw the circle with a compass
Put the compass point on $C(2, -1)$ and open it until the pencil is on $A$.
Turn the compass in a full circle. It also passes through $B$, since $|CB| = |CA|$.
ANSWER: \text{Circle with centre } (2, -1) \text{ through } A \text{ and } B

## Substitute P(2, k) into the circle equation
(x - 2)^2 + (y + 1)^2 &= 25
(2 - 2)^2 + (k + 1)^2 &= 25
0 + (k + 1)^2 &= 25
k^2 + 2k + 1 &= 25
## Solve the quadratic
k^2 + 2k - 24 &= 0
(k + 6)(k - 4) &= 0
k = -6 \ \text{or} \ k &= 4
## Choose the value in the first quadrant
$P$ is in the first quadrant, so $k > 0$ and $k = -6$ is rejected.
k &= 4
## Plot P(2, 4)
Go to $x = 2$ and up to $y = 4$. This is the top of the circle, directly above $C$.
ANSWER: k = 4
